external_entities.name: member
external_entities.description: A person who uses the loyalty programme and may connect a partner app.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Members collect points when they shop
external_entities.notes: The text does not state where the member is located or controlled.

external_entities.name: member phone
external_entities.description: A member's phone on which the mobile app keeps a refresh token.
external_entities.source_excerpt: The app keeps a refresh token on the phone.

external_entities.name: partner app
external_entities.description: A web application run by another company that can access member points.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers

external_entities.name: browser
external_entities.description: A browser used by a member to sign in and approve partner-app access.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A member who connects a partner app signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser
external_entities.notes: The text does not state whether the browser runs on a member phone or another device.

processes.name: mobile app
processes.description: The mobile application that signs members in and calls the rewards API.
processes.notes: The app's PKCE behavior is not documented. A mobile refresh token never expires and its expiry slides forward another ninety days when used.

processes.name: authorization server
processes.description: The server that authenticates members and issues authorization codes, access tokens and refresh tokens.
processes.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes
processes.notes: It signs tokens for the support console with the same key used for other tokens. The sign-in cookie lasts thirty days and no idle timeout was decided.

processes.name: rewards API
processes.description: The API that reads and writes the points ledger and processes gift-card redemptions.
processes.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger
processes.notes: It checks JWT signatures using a public key downloaded at startup, but does not check the token client or audience.

processes.name: support console
processes.description: A web application that closes member accounts.
processes.source_excerpt: The support console is a web app that closes a member's account.

data_stores.name: identity database
data_stores.description: The database containing member identity data and authorization state.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database
data_stores.notes: It also contains authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents, and retains refresh tokens after an account is closed.

data_stores.name: points ledger
data_stores.description: The ledger containing member balances and points transactions.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the points ledger, which holds every member's balance and every points transaction
data_stores.notes: The ledger records which client made each change, but not which member approved it.

data_stores.name: API log store
data_stores.description: The store receiving every request received by the rewards API, including headers.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.
data_stores.notes: The text does not specify the contents of the request bodies or whether headers contain tokens.

data_flows.name: use mobile app
data_flows.description: A member uses the mobile app.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members use our mobile app.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: The mobile app signs a member in using the authorization code flow.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow
data_flows.notes: The source does not state whether the app sends a PKCE challenge.

data_flows.name: call rewards API
data_flows.description: The mobile app calls the rewards API with an access token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: then calls the rewards API with the access token it gets back

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: The browser submits member sign-in and consent interactions to the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A member who connects a partner app signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser and approves a consent screen
data_flows.data_description: member credentials, consent and requested scopes

data_flows.name: request tokens
data_flows.description: The partner app submits token requests to the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The partner app sends that secret in the body of its token requests.
data_flows.notes: The partner app authenticates with a client secret sent in the request body.

data_flows.name: return authorization code
data_flows.description: The browser returns an authorization code to the partner app's redirect URI.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The browser then returns to the partner app's redirect URI with an authorization code.
data_flows.notes: Authorization codes remain valid for ten minutes.

data_flows.name: disconnect partner app
data_flows.description: A member disconnects a partner app, causing its refresh token to be deleted from the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members can disconnect a partner app from the settings screen of the mobile app, which deletes that app's refresh token from the identity database.
data_flows.notes: The member acts through the mobile app, but the described destination of the deletion is the identity database.

data_flows.name: store authorization data
data_flows.description: The authorization server stores member and authorization data in the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database, together with the authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents it issues.
data_flows.data_description: member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents

data_flows.name: update points ledger
data_flows.description: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger
data_flows.notes: The source does not state how the API connects to the ledger.

data_flows.name: write API logs
data_flows.description: The rewards API writes each received request and its headers to the API log store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.

data_flows.name: close account
data_flows.description: The support console marks a member account closed in the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Closing an account marks it closed in the identity database.
data_flows.notes: The member's refresh tokens remain in the database.

trust_boundaries.name: own cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: The cloud account in which the platform components and stores run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Everything below runs in our own cloud account

trust_boundaries.name: members phones
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: apart from the members' phones and the partner apps.

trust_boundaries.name: partner apps own servers
trust_boundaries.description: Servers controlled by the other companies that run partner apps.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers

assumptions.assumption: The rewards API is reachable from the internet because it is served on the same public hostname as the support console.
assumptions.basis: The support console is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.

assumptions.assumption: The support console is reachable from the internet because it is served on a public hostname.
assumptions.basis: The support console is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.

assumptions.assumption: The identity database is confidential because it contains member identity information, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the identity database contains member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents.

assumptions.assumption: The points ledger is confidential because it contains member balances and points transactions.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the points ledger holds every member's balance and every points transaction.
